requirement: Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas` skill whose description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project, naming as signs of one a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{cite}` references in code.
rationale:
structural: The requirement `requirements.cli.overview_skill` has no structural obligation about how code is built. Its clauses are:

- "Habeas MUST bundle a `habeas` skill": this requires that the skill ships. It names no library, type, signature, or delegation. An alternative that ships the skill by a different mechanism or path gives the same result, so the mechanism is discretionary.
- "whose description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project, naming as signs of one a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`, `{test}`, or `{cite}` references in code": this is a content requirement on the skill's description text.

The supplied root, `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md`, is the skill itself. I read it. Its frontmatter has `name: habeas`. Its description begins "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas". It then names a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in its mdBook, and `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references in code. The root therefore satisfies the requirement, and no further implementation root is needed.

behavioral: The requirement `requirements.cli.overview_skill` has two observable obligations. The first is that Habeas bundles a `habeas` skill. The second is that the skill's description tells agents to use it at the start of any work in a Habeas project and names four signs of one: a `habeas` dev-dependency, a `habeas.toml`, `{req}` directives in the book, and `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references in code.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_habeas_skill_is_used_at_the_start_of_any_work_in_a_habeas_project]` covers both.
- **Bundling:** it reads the description through `description("habeas")`. That helper calls `skill_md`, which reads `skill_files("habeas")`. `skill_files` uses `include_str!` on `assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md`, so the skill must exist in the bundled assets for the test to compile. The helper panics if the file has no `description:` line.
- **Start-of-work instruction:** it asserts that the description starts with "Use at the start of any work in a project that tracks requirements with Habeas".
- **Four signs:** it asserts that the description contains each of the four signs: ``a `habeas` dev-dependency``, ``a `habeas.toml` ``, `` `{req}` directives in its mdBook ``, and `` `{impl}`/`{test}`/`{cite}` references in code ``. Each failure message names the missing sign.

A description that left out any of the four signs, or that did not tell agents to use the skill at the start of work, would fail these assertions. I found no unchecked behavioral obligation.
